block_target: Test whether graded fuzzy packet matrices provide causally meaningful coalition geometry between crisp projectors and overlapping workspaces.
claim_boundary: Bounded terminal-action test of fuzzy packet and edge matrices. No biological-brain, functional-awareness, consciousness, sentience, or valence claim.
implemented_capabilities: terminal-only fuzzy membership learning from an anonymous noisy demand cue
positive diagonal fuzzy packet operators forming an exact partition of unity
exact fuzzy transfer-block reconstruction of arbitrary finite operators
covariant packet transport under agent permutation
crisp, familiar-blend, diffuse, and held-out central-interpolation families
causal membership ablation and strength-effect calibration
known_limitations: The model is a four-agent synthetic terminal-action system, not a biological or natural-language agent.
The number of packets, membership matrix shape, gains, cue interface, and task episode boundary are supplied.
The holdout tests unseen central interpolation coefficients over familiar topology pairs, not unseen coalition topology.
The direct-edge model is predictively stronger than the fuzzy packet factorization, so unique predictive superiority is not established.
Crisp tasks become relatively sharper but do not converge to exact learned idempotent projectors.
Uniform idempotence pressure reduces packet defect but increases task error, especially on graded tasks.
No functional-awareness, consciousness, subjective-experience, sentience, valence, or brain-implementation claim follows.
next_unclosed_gap: Learn the number of packets, memberships, and temporal coalition dynamics from continuous raw interaction, including unseen topologies and explicit comparisons against structured attention and graph-learning baselines.

crystallization_exploratory.interpretation: Exploratory uniform idempotence pressure; not a frozen endpoint.
